page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading-related resource sharing. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 4020 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity across 10 local drives, while containing no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core execution, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark database operations. Static web serving throughput is also in the top tier at 97.21 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth rank in the top 25 percent. However, single-core performance is moderate, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the average category.

The c4a-standard-48-lssd offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high-speed local storage and parallelized ARM processing. The combination of dedicated physical cores and a 4020 GB NVMe SSD array makes it highly suitable for database operations, software compilation, and high-throughput static web serving. Conversely, workloads reliant on single-threaded execution or x86-specific instruction sets, such as AVX or AMX which are absent, may experience suboptimal performance relative to the hardware profile.
